articles.title: Authorities seize 800 servers used for cyberattacks and disinformation
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested two men and seized 800 servers used to host cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns allegedly supporting Russian state interests. The operation targeted a hosting provider suspected of violating international sanctions laws by enabling activities aimed at destabilizing democratic and economic systems.

articles.title: FBI warns of Kali365 phishing service targeting Microsoft 365 accounts
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding the Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform, which targets Microsoft 365 accounts by exploiting OAuth device code authentication to steal session tokens and bypass MFA.

articles.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites for ClickFix Attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-26980) in Ghost CMS to inject malicious scripts and facilitate ClickFix attacks across over 700 websites.

articles.title: US states step up cyber defenses to protect local communities
articles.summary: U.S. state governments are actively strengthening cybersecurity for local communities by implementing shared defense programs, regional security centers, and specialized workforce initiatives. These measures aim to enhance regional resilience and reduce costs through centralized services and procurement.

articles.title: The Alert Firehose Finally Meets Its Match
articles.summary: The integration of agentic AI into Network Detection and Response (NDR) tools is successfully addressing long-standing issues with alert fatigue and false positives. This evolution allows security teams to triage incidents more efficiently and identify threats earlier in the lifecycle.

articles.title: Netherlands Busts Bulletproof Hosting Network Linked to Disinformation and Cybercrime
articles.summary: Dutch authorities dismantled a bulletproof hosting network used for cybercrime, disinformation campaigns, and bypassing Russian sanctions. Two suspects were arrested in connection with the operation.

articles.title: Zero-Click WhatsApp Account Takeover Hits iPhone Users Running iOS 16. No Linked Devices, No Warning
articles.summary: A zero-click vulnerability targeting iPhones running iOS 16 allows attackers to hijack WhatsApp accounts without user interaction or linked device notifications. This exploit facilitates unauthorized access, enabling malicious actors to send fraudulent messages from the victim's account.

articles.title: Lazarus Deploys RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Against Financial and Crypto Firms
articles.summary: The North Korean-linked Lazarus Group is utilizing a new cross-platform memory-only malware called RemotePE to target financial and cryptocurrency organizations through a multi-stage infection chain. The operation employs specialized loaders, DPAPILoader and RemotePELoader, to execute the malicious payload.

articles.title: Dutch authorities dismantle hosting network allegedly used for cyberattacks and disinformation
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested two individuals and seized 800 servers associated with Stark Industries, a hosting provider allegedly facilitating cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns. The operation targeted infrastructure suspected of supporting Russian interference activities.

articles.title: Anthropic to release Mythos-class models to the public
articles.summary: Anthropic is expanding access to its Mythos-class AI vulnerability-detection models to government and select users while continuing to develop safety guardrails. The company remains cautious about a full public release to prevent potential misuse of the flaw-finding capabilities.

articles.title: FBI director Kash Patel’s brand website taken offline after malware reports
articles.summary: The merchandise website for FBI Director Kash Patel was taken offline following a compromise that leveraged a fake Cloudflare prompt to execute a ClickFix malware attack on visitors.

articles.title: TrapDoor Supply Chain Attack Spreads Credential-Stealing Malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO
articles.summary: The TrapDoor supply chain attack campaign has compromised over 34 malicious packages across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io to distribute credential-stealing malware. This coordinated effort involves hundreds of malicious package versions impacting multiple software development ecosystems.

articles.title: Lessons for organizations from the Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report
articles.summary: This article highlights the release of the Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report (DBIR) and emphasizes its value as a essential resource for organizations to understand current security threats. It frames the report as a top-tier industry document that provides critical insights for strengthening cybersecurity posture.

articles.title: OpenHack: Open-source AI-powered vulnerability research
articles.summary: Hadrian has released OpenHack, an MIT-licensed, open-source project that utilizes AI agents to automate the vulnerability research process within developer coding harnesses. This tool packages expert-led research methodologies into a workspace compatible with existing AI coding assistants.

articles.title: Boards want cyber risk in dollars, not CVE counts
articles.summary: Security leaders are increasingly pressured to translate complex technical vulnerabilities into financial risk metrics to better communicate with corporate boards. This shift emphasizes mapping cyber threats to critical business assets to justify security investment in terms executives understand.

articles.title: Turns out the C-suite loves shadow AI
articles.summary: A TrustedTech report reveals that senior decision-makers are the primary drivers of shadow AI usage, continuing to utilize unapproved tools despite clear awareness of the associated security and privacy risks. This suggests that shadow AI adoption is a leadership-driven trend rather than a grassroots employee practice.

articles.title: Hacker Selling 340 Million OnlyFans User Records Built From Old Breaches
articles.summary: A threat actor is offering a database of 340 million OnlyFans user records for sale, reportedly aggregated by cross-referencing previous data breaches and public profile information. This incident highlights the risks of credential stuffing and data exposure through the aggregation of legacy breach data.

articles.title: Ghost CMS SQL injection flaw exploited in large-scale ClickFix campaign
articles.summary: A large-scale campaign is actively exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Ghost CMS, identified as CVE-2026-26980, to execute ClickFix malicious JavaScript attacks. The vulnerability enables attackers to inject unauthorized code, posing a significant risk to affected installations.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 98
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights several recent supply chain attacks and malware campaigns targeting npm packages and GitHub actions, emphasizing the growing threat to software development ecosystems. It covers incidents involving credential stealers, Shai-Hulud clones, and compromised development tools.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 578 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Drupal (CVE-2026-9082) that is currently being exploited in the wild, alongside discussions on extortion-based cyberattacks.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Project Glasswing: 10,000+ Vulnerabilities Found in One Month, and the Patching Problem Has Never Been More Obvious
articles.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing, powered by the Claude Mythos Preview, identified over 10,000 critical security vulnerabilities in its first month, highlighting a significant and growing gap in organizational patching capabilities.

articles.title: Week in review: GitHub breached via poisoned VS Code extension, critical NGINX flaw exploited
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed an internal breach caused by a malicious VS Code extension, alongside reports of active exploitation of a critical NGINX vulnerability.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Drupal Core to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include a critical vulnerability in Drupal Core. This action mandates that federal agencies address the security flaw to mitigate potential exploitation risks.

articles.title: Laravel Lang packages hijacked to deploy credential-stealing malware
articles.summary: Attackers compromised Laravel Lang localization packages by abusing GitHub version tags to inject credential-stealing malware into Composer dependencies. This supply chain attack successfully distributed malicious code to developers utilizing the popular localization library.

articles.title: npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing and Package Install Controls Against Supply Chain Attacks
articles.summary: GitHub has introduced staged publishing for npm, requiring two-factor authentication (2FA) and manual approval before package releases become publicly available to mitigate supply chain attacks.

articles.title: CVE-2026-9082: Drupal’s Highly Critical SQL Injection Flaw Is Already Under Active Attack
articles.summary: A highly critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-9082) affecting Drupal sites using PostgreSQL is currently being exploited in the wild shortly after its patch release.

articles.title: Packagist Supply Chain Attack Infects 8 Packages Using GitHub-Hosted Linux Malware
articles.summary: A coordinated supply chain attack compromised eight Packagist packages by injecting malicious code into package.json files to execute Linux binaries from GitHub. The campaign strategically targets projects that ship both PHP and JavaScript components.

articles.title: Italy disrupts CINEMAGOAL piracy app that stole streaming auth codes
articles.summary: Italian authorities dismantled the CINEMAGOAL piracy app, which illegally accessed streaming service authentication tokens to provide unauthorized content distribution. The operation effectively neutralized a significant ecosystem facilitating large-scale digital content theft.

articles.title: Why pure extortion is replacing traditional ransomware
articles.summary: Ransomware gangs are evolving their tactics by moving away from system encryption toward pure data extortion, focusing on stealing sensitive information and threatening public leaks to exert pressure. This shift enables attackers to operate more stealthily while maintaining high leverage over their victims.

articles.title: Claude Mythos AI Finds 10,000 High-Severity Flaws in Widely Used Software
articles.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing initiative has utilized AI to identify over 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in essential global software systems within its first month of operation.

articles.title: RondoDox Botnet Exploits Critical 2018 Vulnerability to Hijack ASUS Routers
articles.summary: The RondoDox botnet is actively leveraging a critical 2018 security vulnerability to bypass authentication and compromise over a million ASUS routers. This campaign highlights the persistent risk posed by unpatched legacy vulnerabilities in network hardware.

articles.title: AI eyes scanning for bugs create a worrisome Linux security trend
articles.summary: The emergence of AI-driven vulnerability discovery tools is accelerating the identification of Linux kernel flaws, such as Dirty Frag and Copy Fail, creating new challenges for system security maintenance. This trend suggests that attackers are increasingly leveraging automated systems to find and exploit vulnerabilities at a faster pace.

articles.title: Dirty Frag, Copy Fail, Fragnesia: The start of a worrisome Linux security trend
articles.summary: The emergence of several Linux-related vulnerabilities nicknamed 'Dirty Frag,' 'Copy Fail,' and 'Fragnesia' signals a potential rise in systematic exploit discovery. The article questions whether these findings are a natural security evolution or an effect of AI-driven vulnerability scanning.

articles.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Malicious actors compromised several Laravel-Lang PHP packages to inject a credential-stealing framework, marking a significant software supply chain attack. Users of the affected packages are at risk of data theft via the compromised tags.

articles.title: Ghostwriter Is Back, Using a Ukrainian Learning Platform as Bait to Hit Government Targets
articles.summary: The Belarus-linked threat actor Ghostwriter has launched a new phishing campaign targeting Ukrainian government employees by spoofing the legitimate Prometheus online learning platform to deliver malware and Cobalt Strike. This resurfacing of the UAC-0057 group highlights a continued focus on critical government infrastructure.

articles.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 Exploited to Run Scripts as Root
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin (CVE-2026-48172) is being actively exploited, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.

articles.title: Drupal Core SQL Injection Bug Actively Exploited, Added to CISA KEV
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-9082) in Drupal Core to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to reports of active exploitation. Organizations using Drupal are urged to apply the latest security patches to mitigate this risk.

articles.title: CISA to allow researchers to report vulnerabilities to exploited bugs catalog
articles.summary: CISA has introduced a new nomination process allowing security researchers and industry partners to directly report vulnerabilities for inclusion in the agency's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. This initiative aims to improve the speed and accuracy of tracking actively exploited security flaws.

articles.title: A Russian speaker and jailbroken Gemini went on a hacking spree and emptied at least one MAGA victim's crypto wallets
articles.summary: A threat actor utilized a jailbroken instance of Google's Gemini AI to facilitate a hacking spree that resulted in the theft of cryptocurrency from targeted victims. The incident highlights the growing risk of adversarial AI being leveraged to assist in malicious cyber activities.

articles.title: FBI warns about fast-growing phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 users
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding Kali365, a phishing kit that exploits Microsoft's legitimate device authorization process to gain persistent, unauthorized access to user accounts. This tool has seen rapid adoption by cybercriminals since its emergence in April.

articles.title: FBI warns of Kali365 phishing-as-a-service after April Microsoft 365 attacks
articles.summary: The FBI has issued an advisory regarding Kali365, a Telegram-based phishing-as-a-service platform used to harvest OAuth tokens for compromising Microsoft 365 environments. The alert follows a series of targeted attacks observed in April.

articles.title: FBI Warns of Kali365 Phishing Service Targeting Microsoft 365 Account
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service platform that enables attackers to bypass multi-factor authentication and compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. This tool simplifies account hijacking by eliminating the need for password-based credentials.

articles.title: Meta settles school district lawsuit claiming addictive design harmed students' mental health
articles.summary: Meta has reached a settlement in the first of over 1,200 lawsuits filed by school districts alleging that the company's social media platforms are designed to be addictive and harmful to student mental health.

articles.title: Megalodon chums the waters in 5.5K+ GitHub repo poisonings
articles.summary: The 'Megalodon' campaign has successfully compromised over 5,500 GitHub repositories by injecting malicious code. This large-scale supply chain attack poses a significant risk to developers and organizations relying on the affected repositories.

articles.title: First VPN Dismantled in Global Takedown Over Use by 25 Ransomware Groups
articles.summary: Authorities in Europe and North America dismantled a criminal VPN service that facilitated ransomware, data theft, and other cyberattacks for at least 25 different threat groups. The operation was led by law enforcement in France and the Netherlands.

articles.title: Netherlands seizes 800 servers of hosting firm enabling cyberattacks
articles.summary: Dutch financial crime investigators arrested two individuals and seized 800 servers from a hosting provider identified as a hub for cyberattacks, disinformation, and digital interference. The operation marks a significant disruption to infrastructure used to facilitate global malicious activities.

articles.title: Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware
articles.summary: The Belarus-aligned threat actor Ghostwriter is conducting phishing campaigns against Ukrainian government entities by leveraging lures related to the Prometheus online learning platform. The activity has been identified and reported by CERT-UA.

articles.title: Former US execs plead guilty to aiding tech support scammers
articles.summary: Two former executives pleaded guilty to facilitating a global tech support fraud scheme by hiding the illicit activities of their clients. The case highlights how corporate entities can be leveraged to sustain large-scale cyber-fraud operations.

articles.title: Why the Supreme Court's Chatrie case could change the meaning of privacy in America
articles.summary: The Supreme Court's evaluation of the Chatrie case regarding geofence searches has the potential to fundamentally redefine privacy rights and legal standards for digital surveillance in the United States.

articles.title: Canadian man arrested, charged for running KimWolf DDos botnet
articles.summary: Canadian national Jacob Butler has been arrested and charged for operating the KimWolf botnet, a DDoS-for-hire service that compromised over one million devices globally. The investigation, led by the U.S. Justice Department, highlights the ongoing crackdown on illicit cybercriminal services.

articles.title: $20 per zero-day is already the WordPress plugin reality
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an automated AI-driven pipeline capable of discovering zero-day vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins at a cost of only $20 per bug. This advancement highlights the growing efficiency of AI in vulnerability research and the potential for a surge in mass-produced software exploits.

articles.title: Authorities arrest 23-year-old accused of running the Kimwolf botnet
articles.summary: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler for allegedly operating the Kimwolf DDoS botnet, with the United States currently seeking his extradition to face criminal charges.

articles.title: 5,561 GitHub Repositories Hit by Megalodon Supply Chain Attack in Six Hours
articles.summary: The Megalodon supply chain attack compromised over 5,500 GitHub repositories within six hours by injecting malicious CI workflows to steal cloud credentials. Researchers at SafeDep discovered the incident, highlighting a significant automated threat to software supply chains.

articles.title: Trend Micro warns of Apex One zero-day exploited in the wild
articles.summary: Trend Micro has released a security update to address a zero-day vulnerability in its Apex One software that is currently being exploited in the wild to target Windows systems.

articles.title: Drupal: Critical SQL injection flaw now targeted in attacks
articles.summary: Drupal has issued a warning that a critical SQL injection vulnerability is currently being actively exploited by attackers. Users are urged to patch their systems immediately to mitigate the risk of compromise.

articles.title: Why Chargebacks are Just One Piece of the Fraud Puzzle
articles.summary: This article explains that financial fraud extends beyond simple chargebacks to include issues like account takeovers and false declines, necessitating a more comprehensive approach to risk management. It advocates for greater visibility to protect both revenue and customer trust.

articles.title: Tracking Iranian APT Screening Serpens’ 2026 Espionage Campaigns
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports that the Iranian APT group Screening Serpens is leveraging AppDomainManager hijacking and new RAT variants to target organizations in the technology and defense sectors. The campaigns demonstrate the group's ongoing evolution in espionage tactics.

articles.title: Deleted Google API keys keep working for up to 23 minutes, researchers warn
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that Google API keys remain functional for up to 23 minutes after deletion, potentially allowing attackers to exploit leaked credentials even after revocation. This delay exposes services and sensitive data to unauthorized access during the window before the key is fully invalidated.

articles.title: Ubiquiti patches three max severity UniFi OS vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Ubiquiti has addressed three critical vulnerabilities in its UniFi OS that could allow unprivileged remote attackers to compromise affected systems. Users are encouraged to apply the released security updates immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

articles.title: Megalodon GitHub Attack Targets 5,561 Repos with Malicious CI/CD Workflows
articles.summary: An automated campaign dubbed Megalodon injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows into over 5,500 repositories within six hours using forged identities to exfiltrate CI environment secrets. The attackers utilized base64-encoded payloads to compromise the software supply chain through automated commits.

articles.title: Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective
articles.summary: This article explores techniques for interacting with Windows kernel mode drivers from user mode, specifically focusing on how to exploit vulnerabilities in drivers that are typically hardware-gated. It aims to assist security researchers in evaluating the exploitability of kernel-level findings without requiring the associated hardware.

articles.title: Techie claims Trump Mobile website was leaking thousands of people's data
articles.summary: A security researcher discovered that the Trump Mobile website was improperly configured, allowing unauthorized access to thousands of customers' sensitive personal data through simple HTTP requests.

articles.title: Kore.ai unveils AI-native platform for enterprise multiagent systems
articles.summary: Kore.ai has launched its new Artemis edition platform, designed to enable enterprises to build, govern, and deploy multiagent AI systems on Microsoft Azure. The platform emphasizes rapid deployment while integrating operational control and observability features.

articles.title: Suspected KimWolf botnet admin arrested over DDoS-for-hire operation
articles.summary: Canadian authorities arrested Jacob Butler, the alleged operator of the KimWolf botnet, which compromised over one million devices to facilitate DDoS-for-hire attacks. He is now facing charges in the United States following an extradition process.

articles.title: Versa extends zero trust principles to AI agents and MCP workflows
articles.summary: Versa has introduced a zero-trust architecture for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to secure AI agent workflows by validating every AI-generated action against identity and access policies. This solution aims to mitigate risks associated with the autonomous actions taken by enterprise AI systems.

articles.title: GitLab 19.0 adds AI workflows, secrets management, and self-hosted model support
articles.summary: GitLab 19.0 introduces new AI-driven workflows, enhanced secrets management, and support for self-hosted models to help engineering teams improve security and pipeline efficiency. These updates address the challenge of scaling secure development practices while integrating AI-powered capabilities into the software supply chain.

articles.title: Proton Pass adds monitored credential sharing for AI agents
articles.summary: Proton Pass has introduced AI access tokens that allow users to securely share specific credentials with AI agents while maintaining oversight through activity monitoring and mandatory reason-tracking. This feature aims to balance AI integration with strict security controls for individual and enterprise users.

articles.title: Paved With Intent: ROADtools and Nation-State Tactics in the Cloud
articles.summary: Threat actors are increasingly misusing the open-source ROADtools framework to conduct unauthorized cloud environment intrusions. The report provides security teams with guidance on identifying and mitigating these malicious activities.

articles.title: CISA’s new KEV nomination form opens reporting to vendors and researchers
articles.summary: CISA has introduced a new online nomination form that streamlines the process for vendors and security researchers to report known exploited vulnerabilities for potential inclusion in its KEV catalog. This initiative aims to improve collaboration and threat intelligence sharing regarding active security threats.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Trend Micro Apex One and Langflow to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has expanded its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog by including critical flaws identified in Trend Micro Apex One and Langflow software. This action mandates that federal agencies address these vulnerabilities to mitigate risks of active exploitation.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 users targeted by new phishing threat that bypasses MFA
articles.summary: The FBI warns of a new Phishing-as-a-Service platform called Kali365 that enables attackers to bypass MFA by stealing Microsoft 365 access tokens via AI-generated phishing campaigns. This platform lowers the technical barrier for cybercriminals to compromise accounts without needing user credentials.

articles.title: Meet Fractal, an OS made for microarchitecture reverse engineering
articles.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers have developed Fractal, a specialized operating system designed to simplify microarchitecture reverse engineering by isolating hardware behavior from OS interference. The tool has already successfully identified previously undocumented vulnerabilities in the Apple M1 branch predictor.

articles.title: US and Canada arrest and charge suspected Kimwolf botnet admin
articles.summary: Authorities in the U.S. and Canada have arrested a Canadian individual accused of operating the KimWolf botnet, which compromised nearly two million devices globally for DDoS attacks.

articles.title: Kimwolf DDoS Botnet Operator Arrested in Canada Over DDoS-for-Hire Attacks
articles.summary: A 23-year-old Canadian man was arrested and charged for developing and operating the Kimwolf DDoS botnet, a variant of the AISURU malware used for DDoS-for-hire attacks. The operation was a collaborative effort involving international law enforcement agencies.

articles.title: One Telecom Provider Hosted Most of the Middle East ’s Active C2 Infrastructure
articles.summary: A report from Hunt.io reveals that a single telecom provider hosts a significant portion of active command-and-control (C2) infrastructure across the Middle East, highlighting a strategic shift toward monitoring hosting providers. This discovery emphasizes the need for defenders to focus on infrastructure-level indicators rather than just individual malware samples.

articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited Langflow and Trend Micro Apex One Vulnerabilities to KEV
articles.summary: CISA has added two actively exploited vulnerabilities in Langflow and Trend Micro Apex One to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring immediate remediation. The Langflow vulnerability, CVE-2025-34291, carries a critical CVSS score of 9.4.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Cisco's attempt to automate security incident reporting using AI yielded inconsistent results, requiring complex prompts and remaining prone to errors. This highlights the limitations of current generative AI in producing accurate, technical documentation without manual oversight.

articles.title: Cisco Patches CVSS 10.0 Secure Workload REST API Flaw Enabling Data Access
articles.summary: Cisco has released patches for a critical CVSS 10.0 vulnerability in its Secure Workload REST API that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access sensitive data due to improper authentication and validation. Users are urged to update their systems to mitigate the risk of unauthorized data exposure.

articles.title: Downtime has become a $600 billion business problem
articles.summary: Global 2000 companies are facing an increasing financial impact from unplanned downtime, with costs reaching $600 billion due to service outages and degradation. This represents a 50% rise over two years, resulting in significant business consequences like stock decline and brand damage.

articles.title: The new economics of fraud: Cheaper, faster, more convincing
articles.summary: Visa’s Spring 2026 report highlights how AI-driven social engineering and impersonation are making scams faster and more effective, despite improvements in core payment defenses. The shift focuses on manipulating users into authorizing payments rather than technical system exploits.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: May 22, 2026
articles.summary: Babel Street has introduced 'Insights Investigator,' an AI-driven tool designed to assist investigators by automating tradecraft workflows while maintaining human oversight. This release is part of a weekly roundup of new cybersecurity products.

articles.title: Alleged leader of Kimwolf, a sweeping botnet for cybercriminals, arrested in Canada
articles.summary: Jacob Butler, the 23-year-old alleged leader of the Kimwolf botnet, has been arrested in Canada and faces extradition to the United States. He is charged with orchestrating a significant cybercriminal operation involving the botnet.

articles.title: Dems slam Trump for making cybersecurity hold out the tin cup while splurging on ballroom and Jan. 6 'slush fund'
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers are criticizing former President Trump for prioritizing personal expenditures over funding for critical cybersecurity initiatives. They argue that insufficient budgetary allocations for cybersecurity reflect a failure to prioritize national digital security.

articles.title: Belarus-linked hackers use fake training certificates to target Ukrainian officials
articles.summary: The Belarus-linked threat actor GhostWriter is targeting Ukrainian officials with a spear-phishing campaign that uses counterfeit training certificates to distribute malware. This espionage effort leverages social engineering to compromise sensitive government accounts.

articles.title: Hackers steal patient and billing data from German hospitals via third-party provider
articles.summary: Hackers compromised a third-party billing provider called Unimed, resulting in a large-scale data breach involving patient and billing information across multiple German hospitals.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Microsoft and Adobe flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include specific security flaws found in Microsoft, Adobe, and ConnectWise software. These additions mandate that federal agencies patch the affected systems to mitigate risks from active exploitation.

articles.title: Threat hunters find Google API keys still usable 23 minutes after deletion
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered that deleted Google API keys remain functional for 23 minutes, creating a window of opportunity for unauthorized data access or billing abuse. This latency highlights a critical vulnerability in credential lifecycle management for cloud services.

articles.title: Lawmakers from both parties say CISA cuts have gone too far
articles.summary: Bipartisan lawmakers are raising concerns that recent budget cuts to CISA have weakened the agency's ability to protect civilian networks against increasing cyber threats. They argue these reductions are ill-timed given the escalating risk from nation-state actors like China.

articles.title: HackerOne takes an axe to its bug bounty rewards
articles.summary: HackerOne has significantly reduced its bounty payouts for critical vulnerabilities, slashing compensation by over 75%.

articles.title: Tech giants promise British regulator they will tweak platforms to protect kids online
articles.summary: Major tech companies have committed to Ofcom to modify their platforms to enhance protections for minors, including addressing harmful algorithms and age verification. This follows regulatory pressure to mitigate online risks such as exposure to sexual predators.

articles.title: Trump postpones executive order focused on AI security
articles.summary: The Trump administration has delayed a draft executive order that would have mandated federal agencies to conduct 90-day cybersecurity and national security assessments on new AI models.

articles.title: Google accidentally exposed details of unfixed Chromium flaw
articles.summary: Google inadvertently disclosed an unfixed Chromium vulnerability that permits remote code execution by keeping JavaScript processes active after the browser is closed. This oversight exposes a significant security risk for users until a patch is released.

articles.title: Two Americans plead guilty to assisting India-based tech support scam centers
articles.summary: Two American men pleaded guilty to facilitating India-based tech support scams by providing essential telecommunications infrastructure and call routing services to criminal operators. This case highlights the role of intermediaries in supporting international telemarketing fraud networks.

articles.title: Global law enforcement operation takes First VPN offline
articles.summary: An international law enforcement operation seized the infrastructure of First VPN, a service widely used by cybercriminals for ransomware and data theft activities. The operation resulted in the shutdown of the platform and the exposure of its malicious user base.

articles.title: Apple Blocks Over 2 Million Apps in 2025 Fraud Crackdown
articles.summary: Apple's 2025 fraud prevention report highlights a massive security effort, including the rejection of over 2 million malicious apps and the blocking of 1 billion fake accounts. These measures are designed to mitigate large-scale fraudulent activity and maintain App Store integrity.

articles.title: CISA chief frets about open-source vulnerabilities, delayed security improvements
articles.summary: CISA officials are expressing concerns regarding the inherent security risks in open-source software and the slow pace of implementing necessary security improvements. This follows a recent increase in malware campaigns targeting collaborative technology platforms.

articles.title: Microsoft open-sources tools for designing and testing AI agents
articles.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced its internal tools, Clarity and RAMPART, to help developers implement structured design reviews and continuous security testing for AI agents. These tools, derived from the company's AI Red Team, aim to enhance the security posture of AI system development.

articles.title: European authorities take down prolific cybercrime VPN service
articles.summary: European law enforcement authorities dismantled the 'First VPN' service, arresting its administrator and seizing its digital infrastructure after linking it to numerous major cybercrime investigations.

articles.title: Deleted Google API Keys Remain Active up to 23 Minutes, Study Finds
articles.summary: A study reveals that deleted Google API keys stay functional for up to 23 minutes, creating a window of vulnerability for GCP, Gemini, BigQuery, and Maps services. This latency in key revocation could allow attackers to exploit credentials that administrators believe have been invalidated.

articles.title: Apple blocked over $11 billion in App Store fraud in 6 years
articles.summary: Apple reported preventing over $11 billion in fraudulent App Store transactions over a six-year period, with $2.2 billion blocked in 2025 alone. This disclosure highlights the ongoing challenge of combating financial fraud and illicit activities within digital app marketplaces.

articles.title: UK plans for cybercrime law reform would protect almost no one, experts warn
articles.summary: Experts warn that proposed UK cybercrime law reforms would hinder security researchers by forcing them to halt investigations prematurely upon identifying potential vulnerabilities. This restriction prevents researchers from verifying, assessing, or determining the exploitability of critical security flaws.

articles.title: Attackers are bypassing MFA on SonicWall VPNs because something was wrong with previous fix
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting SonicWall Gen6 VPNs by bypassing MFA, as administrators failed to complete all required manual steps for a previously issued patch. This highlights the critical risk of incomplete remediation processes in security maintenance.

articles.title: Showboat Linux Malware Hits Middle East Telecom with SOCKS5 Proxy Backdoor
articles.summary: The Showboat modular Linux malware has been identified in a long-running campaign targeting Middle Eastern telecommunications infrastructure to establish remote access and SOCKS5 proxy capabilities. Researchers report the framework has been active since at least 2022, facilitating file transfers and shell access for post-exploitation activities.

articles.title: Authorities dismantle First VPN, used by ransomware actors
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies from France, the Netherlands, and Europol dismantled the First VPN service, which was specifically marketed to and utilized by ransomware actors to maintain anonymity. The operation involved seizing 33 servers and shutting down associated domains to disrupt the infrastructure supporting cybercriminal activities.

articles.title: Inside a Crypto Drainer: How to Spot it Before it Empties Your Wallet
articles.summary: This article examines the operational mechanics of the Lucifer DaaS platform, which facilitates large-scale cryptocurrency theft by tricking users into signing malicious transactions. It provides insights into how modern crypto drainers leverage automation and social engineering to bypass wallet security.

articles.title: Chinese hackers target telcos with new Linux, Windows malware
articles.summary: Chinese state-sponsored actors are targeting telecommunications providers using new, platform-specific malware variants identified as Showboat and JFMBackdoor. These tools are designed to facilitate ongoing cyber-espionage activities against critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Max severity Cisco Secure Workload flaw gives Site Admin privileges
articles.summary: Cisco has issued security updates for a critical vulnerability in Secure Workload that permits unauthenticated attackers to escalate privileges to a Site Admin level.

articles.title: GitHub, Grafana Labs breaches traced back to TanStack supply chain compromise
articles.summary: GitHub and Grafana Labs suffered security breaches after threat group TeamPCP injected malicious code into the popular Nx Console VS Code extension. This supply chain attack allowed attackers to steal credentials, infiltrate CI/CD pipelines, and exfiltrate thousands of private GitHub repositories.

articles.title: Cisco fixed maximum severity flaw CVE-2026-20223 in Secure Workload
articles.summary: Cisco has released patches for a maximum severity (CVSS 10.0) vulnerability in its Secure Workload product, which could allow remote attackers to gain unauthorized Site Admin privileges via crafted API requests.

articles.title: Police seize “First VPN” service used in ransomware, data theft attacks
articles.summary: International law enforcement agencies have shut down 'First VPN,' a service frequently utilized by cybercriminals to facilitate ransomware deployments and data theft operations.

articles.title: Europol Seizes First VPN Used by Ransomware Gangs, Arrests Administrator
articles.summary: Europol has dismantled First VPN, a service frequently exploited by ransomware gangs, resulting in the arrest of its administrator and the seizure of user data. This operation significantly disrupts the infrastructure used by cybercriminals to facilitate malicious activities.

articles.title: Attackers spill plaintext passwords of 46k Myspace93 users after 2021 breach
articles.summary: Approximately 46,000 Myspace93 users had their unencrypted passwords and email addresses exposed following a 2021 data breach. The incident was attributed to unauthorized access through compromised internal connections.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Linux Rootkits, Router 0-Day, AI Intrusions, Scam Kits and 25 New Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin highlights an evolving threat landscape where attackers are increasingly exploiting trusted systems, cloud services, and standard software updates rather than just traditional infiltration methods. The report emphasizes the risk posed by compromised legitimate infrastructure, including AI-driven intrusions and router vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Android Malware Spotted Subscribing Victims to Paid Services Without Consent
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a widespread Android malware campaign that uses deceptive applications to enroll unsuspecting users in paid premium SMS services without their authorization. This long-running operation has impacted users globally by generating unauthorized financial charges.

articles.title: Cisco serves up yet another perfect 10 bug with Secure Workload admin flaw
articles.summary: Cisco has patched a critical vulnerability in its Secure Workload platform that could allow unauthorized actors to access sensitive data and modify configurations across tenant boundaries. This flaw stems from a security issue within internal APIs and carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0.

articles.title: Flipper One project needs community help to build open Linux platform
articles.summary: Flipper Devices is seeking community collaboration to develop Flipper One, an open Linux-based platform aimed at connected device research. This initiative expands the company's ecosystem beyond their existing Flipper Zero pentesting tool.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-41091, CVE-2026-45498)
articles.summary: Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities CVE-2026-41091 and CVE-2026-45498 are being actively exploited in the wild, with the former allowing local privilege elevation to SYSTEM level. CISA has added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Two Actively Exploited Defender Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation of two vulnerabilities in Microsoft Defender, including a high-severity privilege escalation flaw that grants attackers SYSTEM access. Users are advised to monitor for updates to mitigate these security risks.

articles.title: When Identity is the Attack Path
articles.summary: This article highlights how common, legitimate credential caching behaviors in cloud environments can be exploited by attackers to gain extensive unauthorized access. It emphasizes that standard security configurations may not prevent identity-based attacks that leverage stored keys to compromise critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Microsoft storms RAMPART, adds Clarity to agentic AI safety
articles.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced RAMPART and Clarity, two new tools designed to enhance the security, safety, and evaluation of agentic AI systems. These resources aim to help developers build more resilient agents by providing frameworks for monitoring and testing.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Retired IE Tool MSHTA Now Being Used in Fileless Malware Attacks
articles.summary: Hackers are exploiting the retired MSHTA utility to execute stealthy, fileless malware attacks on Windows systems. This technique persists despite Microsoft's official retirement of Internet Explorer.

articles.title: The readiness paradox: Why a false sense of cyber confidence is becoming a liability
articles.summary: The rise of AI-driven threats and alert fatigue necessitates a shift toward proactive cyber exposure management to address the dangers of overconfidence. Organizations must move beyond a false sense of security to accurately identify and mitigate concentrated risks before they result in a crisis.

articles.title: Virtru centers file collaboration around data-level protection
articles.summary: Virtru has launched Virtru Collaborate, a FedRAMP-authorized platform that utilizes the Trusted Data Format (TDF) to provide persistent, data-level encryption and policy enforcement for secure file collaboration. This solution is the first to be built on the new Virtru Platform architecture, designed to maintain protection as files are shared across organizational boundaries.

articles.title: ASAPP expands adversarial testing for enterprise AI systems
articles.summary: ASAPP has introduced 'Continuous Red Teaming,' a new feature utilizing the Promptfoo platform to conduct automated adversarial testing for AI systems. This initiative aims to detect over 50 types of AI vulnerabilities in real-time to enhance production security and reliability.

articles.title: Tenable Hexa AI automates remediation across attack surfaces
articles.summary: Tenable has launched Hexa AI, an agentic AI engine integrated into the Tenable One Exposure Management Platform to automate vulnerability remediation and risk reduction. The tool utilizes multi-step reasoning and Model Context Protocol support to streamline security workflows and address complex attack surfaces.

articles.title: Microsoft warns of new Defender zero-days exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft has released security patches to address two zero-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Defender that are currently being exploited by attackers. Users are urged to update their systems to mitigate potential threats.

articles.title: Riverbed introduces new Aternity tools for autonomous IT operations
articles.summary: Riverbed has launched new Aternity capabilities aimed at enabling autonomous IT operations and improving digital experience management through automation and enhanced visibility. The tools are designed to shift IT teams toward proactive, prevention-focused workflows to ensure business continuity.

articles.title: Forward launches Predict to test network changes before deployment
articles.summary: Forward has introduced a new capability called Forward Predict, which utilizes a digital twin of a network to simulate and evaluate the impact of changes before they are deployed to production. This tool aims to enhance network security and stability by identifying potential issues in a pre-deployment environment.

articles.title: 9-Year-Old Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Root Command Execution on Major Distros
articles.summary: A long-standing Linux kernel vulnerability has been discovered that allows unprivileged local users to perform unauthorized privilege escalation and execute commands as root. The flaw has persisted undetected for nine years and affects default installations of major Linux distributions.

articles.title: CTERA brings AI insights and automation for unstructured data
articles.summary: CTERA has launched CTERA InsightAI, an agentic AI intelligence layer designed to enhance data observability by automating the identification of security risks, unusual behaviors, and operational inefficiencies within unstructured data. The platform aims to provide enterprises with real-time insights to better manage and secure large-scale data environments.

articles.title: Terra adds continuous network exploitation validation to its platform
articles.summary: Terra Security has expanded its platform's offensive security capabilities to include continuous network exploitation validation, extending its reach beyond web applications and AI. This new feature allows customers to automatically test the resilience of their network infrastructure against potential exploits.

articles.title: Zombie user account let hackers control the city’s water
articles.summary: Hackers gained unauthorized control over a city's water infrastructure by exploiting a neglected user account that belonged to a former employee. The incident highlights the critical importance of effective offboarding processes to prevent unauthorized access.

articles.title: GitHub links repo breach to TanStack npm supply-chain attack
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed that hackers accessed over 3,800 internal repositories by leveraging a malicious version of the Nx Console VS Code extension, which was compromised through a supply-chain attack on the TanStack npm package. This incident highlights the significant risks posed by compromised developer tools within the software supply chain.

articles.title: Discord adds end-to-end encryption to voice and video calls by default
articles.summary: Discord has implemented end-to-end encryption by default for all voice and video calls, ensuring that conversations remain private and inaccessible to the platform provider. This change was applied automatically to all users without requiring manual configuration or prior notification.

articles.title: GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension
articles.summary: GitHub suffered an internal repository breach after an employee's device was compromised by a malicious version of the Nx Console VS Code extension. The attack originated from a prior compromise of an Nx developer's system.

articles.title: Cyber threats push SMBs to spend more on security
articles.summary: Small and medium-sized businesses are increasing their cybersecurity budgets in response to rising threats and the integration of artificial intelligence. Despite the increased investment, many organizations continue to rely on reactive security measures.

articles.title: Highly Critical Drupal Core Flaw Exposes PostgreSQL Sites to RCE Attacks
articles.summary: Drupal has issued security updates to address a critical vulnerability in its database abstraction API that could allow attackers to execute remote code, escalate privileges, or access sensitive information on PostgreSQL-based sites. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-9082.

articles.title: Europe dismantles VPN service used by cybercriminals to hide ransomware attacks
articles.summary: International law enforcement successfully dismantled First VPN, a service widely used by ransomware operators to obfuscate their activities on criminal forums. The operation aims to disrupt the infrastructure facilitating major cyberattacks.

articles.title: Xi and Putin pledge closer cooperation on AI, cyberspace and satellite systems
articles.summary: Russia and China have announced a strategic partnership to develop independent technological ecosystems in AI, satellite systems, and software to reduce reliance on Western infrastructure. This alignment signals a shift in global technological power dynamics aimed at countering policies from nations deemed unfriendly.

articles.title: Ukraine identifies infostealer operator tied to 28,000 stolen accounts
articles.summary: Ukrainian cyberpolice and U.S. law enforcement have identified an 18-year-old suspect in Odesa for operating an infostealer malware campaign that compromised 28,000 accounts. The operation specifically targeted customers of a California-based online store.

articles.title: Hackers bypass SonicWall VPN MFA due to incomplete patching
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting incomplete patches on SonicWall Gen6 SSL-VPN appliances to brute-force credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication for ransomware deployment. Organizations are urged to ensure their devices are fully updated to mitigate this unauthorized access.

articles.title: Even Claude agrees: hole in its sandbox was real and dangerous
articles.summary: An undisclosed and potentially dangerous sandbox vulnerability in the Claude AI model was identified and silently patched without a formal CVE or public disclosure. The lack of transparency regarding this security flaw highlights concerns about silent remediation practices in AI infrastructure.

articles.title: PinTheft: Another Linux Privilege Escalation, Another Working Exploit, This Time Targeting Arch
articles.summary: PinTheft is a newly identified local privilege escalation vulnerability within the Linux RDS subsystem that currently has publicly available exploit code. Arch Linux users are at the highest risk and are urged to apply patches immediately to mitigate the threat.

articles.title: Meet Rampart and Clarity, Microsoft’s new red team combo AI agents
articles.summary: Microsoft has open-sourced two new AI agents, Rampart and Clarity, designed to assist developers and incident responders in red-teaming security operations. These tools aim to improve automated threat detection and proactive defense testing.

articles.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated May 20)
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides an updated analysis of the evolving npm supply chain threat landscape, highlighting sophisticated tactics such as wormable malware and CI/CD persistence. The report outlines emerging attack vectors and necessary mitigation strategies for developers and organizations.

articles.title: FTC warns 12 major tech firms of violating Take It Down Act
articles.summary: The FTC has issued warnings to 12 major tech companies regarding their compliance with the Take It Down Act, which requires the removal of nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours of a request. This action emphasizes the regulatory pressure on platforms to improve user safety and content moderation practices.

articles.title: Microsoft Open-Sources RAMPART and Clarity to Secure AI Agents During Development
articles.summary: Microsoft has released two open-source tools, RAMPART and Clarity, designed to help developers test and secure AI agents against potential security risks. These frameworks facilitate automated safety testing during the AI development lifecycle.

articles.title: Ukraine probes teen suspect in cyber theft scheme targeting California online shoppers
articles.summary: Ukrainian authorities are investigating a teenage suspect linked to a cyber theft scheme targeting online shoppers in California. The case originated from intelligence shared by U.S. officials regarding hackers operating within Ukraine.

articles.title: Discord migrates all users to end-to-end encryption by default
articles.summary: Discord has transitioned all user messaging to default end-to-end encryption, bucking a trend seen in other social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok.

articles.title: 7-Eleven confirms breach after ShinyHunters claims
articles.summary: 7-Eleven confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to systems containing franchisee documents after the ShinyHunters threat group claimed responsibility. The incident was discovered on April 8, prompting an internal investigation into the exposure.

articles.title: Grafana breach caused by missed token rotation after TanStack attack
articles.summary: Grafana experienced a data breach resulting from a failure to rotate a GitHub workflow token following the recent TanStack npm supply-chain attack. The oversight allowed unauthorized access due to a remaining valid credential that should have been revoked.

articles.title: Microsoft issues YellowKey mitigation, no patch yet
articles.summary: Microsoft has released manual mitigations for the YellowKey BitLocker bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-45585) instead of a formal software patch. Users are advised to disable autofstx.exe and enable TPM+PIN to secure their systems.

articles.title: Understanding Trend Structure: Higher Highs and Lower Lows Explained
articles.summary: This article discusses technical market analysis techniques regarding price structure, such as higher highs and lower lows. It does not contain information related to cybersecurity.

articles.title: GitHub says internal repositories were impacted in poisoned VS Code extension attack
articles.summary: GitHub experienced a data breach involving internal repositories after an employee's device was compromised by a malicious Visual Studio Code extension. The incident highlights the escalating security risks associated with third-party developer tools within software development ecosystems.

articles.title: Microsoft Takes Down Malware-Signing Service Behind Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft disrupted a malware-signing-as-a-service operation run by the threat actor Fox Tempest that abused legitimate signing systems to distribute ransomware. The operation impacted thousands of global networks and devices.

articles.title: Webworm APT targets European government organizations with new backdoors
articles.summary: The China-aligned APT group Webworm, also known as Space Pirates, has expanded its cyber espionage operations to target government organizations across Europe and a university in South Africa using new backdoors. The activity was uncovered by ESET, highlighting the group's evolving geographic reach since its inception in 2022.

articles.title: Verizon DBIR: Vulnerability exploitation is the dominant initial access vector
articles.summary: The 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report reveals that vulnerability exploitation has surpassed stolen credentials as the primary method for initial network access. This shift marks the first time in 19 years that credential theft has not been the leading vector for cyberattacks.

articles.title: Identity Alone Isn't Enough: Why Device Security Has to Share the Load
articles.summary: The headline highlights that identity-based authentication is no longer sufficient to secure networks against modern threats, emphasizing the necessity of integrating continuous device verification within Zero Trust architectures. It notes that attackers are increasingly bypassing identity checks by exploiting compromised devices and stolen session tokens.

articles.title: NanoCo lands $12 million seed funding, launches enterprise assistant built on NanoClaw
articles.summary: NanoCo has secured $12 million in seed funding and launched an enterprise-grade professional assistant leveraging its open-source agent framework, NanoClaw.

articles.title: GitHub Breach: TeamPCP Steals 3,800 Repositories via VS Code Extension
articles.summary: The threat group TeamPCP compromised 3,800 GitHub repositories using a malicious VS Code extension and is currently offering the stolen data for sale on the dark web for $95,000.

articles.title: Texas, Florida top list of states reporting millions of dollars lost through crypto ATMs
articles.summary: Residents in Texas and Florida have reported significant financial losses due to scams involving cryptocurrency ATMs, where fraudsters guide victims through the process of transferring funds. These incidents highlight the increasing use of physical kiosks as a common vector for financial fraud.

articles.title: Drupal critical update to fix bug with high exploitation risk
articles.summary: Drupal has scheduled a critical core security release to address a vulnerability with a high risk of exploitation. The organization warns that threat actors may attempt to create exploits shortly after the patch is disclosed.

articles.title: Webworm Deploys EchoCreep and GraphWorm Backdoors Using Discord and MS Graph API
articles.summary: The China-aligned threat actor Webworm is utilizing custom EchoCreep and GraphWorm backdoors that leverage Discord and Microsoft Graph API for command-and-control communications against government targets.

articles.title: Verizon DBIR: AI Helped Hackers Exploit Vulnerabilities in 31% of Recent Breaches
articles.summary: The 2026 Verizon DBIR report highlights that software vulnerabilities have surpassed compromised passwords as the primary attack vector, with AI significantly accelerating the speed at which hackers exploit these flaws. This shift underscores a critical increase in the efficiency and frequency of automated exploitation campaigns.

articles.title: GitHub confirms being hacked by TeamPCP, says customer data unaffected
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed a security breach where hackers known as TeamPCP claimed to have stolen source code from the platform. The company stated that no customer data was compromised during the incident.

articles.title: Carding site B1ack’s Stash dumps 4.6 Million stolen cards for free
articles.summary: The dark web marketplace B1ack’s Stash has leaked 4.6 million stolen credit card records for free following a decision to suspend its seller operations. This mass release of financial data poses a significant risk of widespread payment fraud for the affected consumers.

articles.title: Senator presses CISA for answers about alleged GitHub repository leak
articles.summary: Senator Maggie Hassan has demanded an explanation from CISA regarding a reported data breach involving government contractor Nightwing, which was first exposed by journalist Brian Krebs. The inquiry seeks to understand the scope and implications of an alleged leak from a GitHub repository.

articles.title: Agent AI is Coming. Are You Ready?
articles.summary: Orchid Security's 2026 report reveals that unmanaged 'identity dark matter' now outweighs visible identity components, creating significant security risks for enterprises rapidly adopting Agent AI. This gap suggests organizations are unprepared for the identity management challenges posed by new AI deployments.

articles.title: FBI: $388 million lost in crypto ATM scams in 2026
articles.summary: The FBI reports that Americans lost over $388 million to cryptocurrency ATM scams in 2025, as criminals increasingly use these physical kiosks to facilitate fraudulent fund transfers. The agency warns of the growing exploitation of these machines due to their high visibility and accessibility in public locations.

articles.title: ArmorCode gives security teams AI workers for exposure and remediation
articles.summary: ArmorCode has launched Anya Agents, an AI-driven framework designed to automate security workflows including triage, vulnerability remediation, and compliance at enterprise scale. The platform utilizes a Context Risk Graph to convert security data into actionable tasks for automated AI workers.

articles.title: Novata uses AI to map risk across portfolios and supply chains
articles.summary: Novata has launched Risk Atlas, an AI-powered monitoring tool designed to help organizations aggregate, normalize, and prioritize risk signals across their portfolios and supply chains.

articles.title: Fake Word Phishing Reveals Enterprise Blind Spot in Trusted Remote Access Tools
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered a phishing campaign using fake Microsoft Word documents to exploit trusted remote access tools and bypass enterprise security. The attack highlights a significant blind spot in how organizations monitor and authorize legitimate administrative software.

articles.title: Exploit released for new PinTheft Arch Linux root escalation flaw
articles.summary: A public proof-of-concept exploit has been released for the PinTheft vulnerability, enabling local attackers to achieve root escalation on Arch Linux systems.

articles.title: TeamPCP breached GitHub’s internal codebase via poisoned VS Code extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP gained unauthorized access to GitHub's internal private repositories by utilizing a malicious VS Code extension. GitHub confirmed the breach, noting that the exfiltration was limited to internal source code and did not impact customer information.

articles.title: Typosquatting Is No Longer a User Problem. It's a Supply Chain Problem
articles.summary: Attackers are now leveraging AI-generated lookalike domains embedded within third-party scripts, shifting typosquatting from a user-based threat to a supply chain security risk. Current security stacks often fail to detect these obfuscated threats, necessitating more advanced monitoring techniques.

articles.title: GitHub says internal repos exfiltrated after poisoned VS Code extension attack
articles.summary: GitHub reported that unauthorized actors exfiltrated internal repositories after compromising developer accounts via a malicious VS Code extension. While the company stated that customer data remains secure, the incident has raised concerns regarding the extent of the unauthorized access.

articles.title: Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports on TamperedChef malware, which utilizes trojanized applications and malvertising tactics to deploy stealthy payloads. The analysis tracks these clusters through identified patterns in code and certificate reuse.
